rv.q: Igor Golyak’s genius — it doesn’t seem too strong a word at this point — is to bring not just form and brio but the flavor of originality to some of the most complex and demanding material the theater has to offer.
Arlekin Players’ riotous, rampantly imaginative, and deeply moving production, Delirium , is a new adaptation of Ionesco’s Frenzy for Two helmed by Arlekin’s Artistic Director, Igor Golyak.
Delirium is one of the bravest productions I’ve seen since Dybbuk (also by Arlekin Players).
Delirium is hilarious and deeply disturbing.

Delirium not only testifies to the superb skills of Golyak, his production team, and its cast, but also to the resonant power of the theater of the absurd as we (hopefully) move through the age of polycrisis .
Delirium is as unpredictable and funny as it is stirring and startling.

cn.t: Critics unanimously praise Arlekin's "Delirium" as an imaginative, high-energy adaptation of Ionesco's absurdist work that resonates powerfully with contemporary chaos, featuring exceptional comedic performances and boundless creativity.
